title: Stop double-booking seats on a shared seat map

blocks.text: An airline keeps seat holds for each flight in one `ConcurrentHashMap` from seat to customer. Every booking request builds its own `SeatHolds` over the flight's map, so requests for the same seat run on different threads at the same moment. Two support tickets came in this week:

items: "Both my wife and I got a confirmation for 31F. At the gate the system had only her name."
"I held 5B, then someone else's cancellation freed my seat. They had clicked Release twice."

blocks.text: `holderOf(...)` already works. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/SeatHolds.java`:

items: `reserve(seat, customer)`: true when this customer now holds the seat;
`release(seat, customer)`: true when this customer's hold was removed.

blocks.text: When you're done, two requests that race for one free seat give it to exactly one customer, a refused request changes nothing, and a release that arrives late never frees someone else's seat. About two lines in total.
The tests use a map that pauses one request right after it reads, while another request runs.

cases.says: a free seat goes to the customer who asks for it, and a taken seat is refused
a customer can release their own hold, and nobody else's
when two requests for one free seat meet, exactly one is told yes and the map names that customer
a refused request leaves the seat with the customer who holds it
a release that arrives after the seat went to someone else leaves the new hold in place

origin.section: Code With No Data Race Can Still Race: a Check and an Act Are Two Steps

concepts: One atomic call (putIfAbsent, remove(key, value), compareAndSet, compute) decides between racing threads; a check followed by a separate act does not.
